neighbours.label: the article ' a' that introduces a hand tool or utensil in an instruction ('using a box grater', 'with a fork'), as against ' a' before an ingredient or amount in the same recipe style
fire: Peel the carrots and slice them thinly using a mandoline.
Crush the garlic cloves with a knife before adding them to the pan.
Beat the eggs in a jug using a whisk until they are frothy.
Roll out the pastry with a rolling pin to an even thickness.
Zest the lemon using a microplane, avoiding the bitter pith.
Strain the stock through a sieve and discard the bones.
Crack the walnuts with a nutcracker and pick out the meat.
Flatten the chicken breasts using a mallet until they are thin.
quiet: Peel the carrots and add a pinch of salt to the water.
Crush the garlic cloves and add a splash of olive oil to the pan.
Beat the eggs in a jug and stir in a spoonful of cream.
Roll out the pastry and sprinkle a little flour over the top.
Zest the lemon and squeeze a few drops of juice into the bowl.
Strain the stock and stir in a knob of butter at the end.
Crack the walnuts and add a handful of raisins to the mix.
Flatten the chicken breasts and season them with a dash of pepper.

predictions: fire 0.3-1.0 on ' a' before a utensil after using/with/like; ' a' before ingredients or quantities 0.0-0.2
short: article before an instrument in instructions
notes: Card peaks on ' a' in 'using| a box grater', 'with| a spoon', 'like| a hole punch', plus French pieces. Probe: 'using a box grater' 1.030, 'with a fork' 0.622, 'like a hole punch' 0.303, 'with a spoon' 0.169; same grate sentence without the tool 0.235 (on ' the'), 'bought a new car' -0.001. The spoon case is weak, so the label may hold only for some tools.
